title: Function field and normalization of a normal two-root chart model
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a field, let $U$ be an integral scheme of finite type over $k_0$, and put $K=k(U)$ [def-weil-field, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sc-function-field]. Let $n\geq1$, let $Y$ be an integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed domains, and let $q:Y\to P=\mathbf P^1_U$ be a finite surjective $U$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Suppose that for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset U$, the inverse images of the standard $x$- and $y$-charts of $P_V$ are affine, with identifications over those charts
$$S_C=R[x,a,b]/(a^n-x,b^n-(x-1)),\qquad S_A=R[y,u,v]/(v^n-y,u^n-(1-y)).$$
Assume that these presentations commute with restriction to base opens and that on their overlap $y=x^{-1}$, $v=a^{-1}$, $u=b/a$. Then $P$ is integral and $k(P)=K(x)$ with the embedding of $K$ induced by $P\to U$. Under the inclusion $k(P)\hookrightarrow k(Y)$ induced by $q$, there are generators $a,b$ represented by the indicated chart coordinates such that
$$k(Y)=K(x)(a,b),\qquad a^n=x,\qquad b^n=x-1,$$
and this is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. For every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset U$, on each displayed target affine chart of $P_V$ the corresponding $S_C$ or $S_A$ is an integrally closed domain with fraction field $k(Y)$ and is exactly the integral closure of its target ring $R[x]$ or $R[y]$ in that field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. These identifications agree on overlaps and identify $q$ over $P$ with the normalization of $P$ in $k(Y)$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. No smoothness, primality of $n$, primitive root of unity or normality hypothesis on $U$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the two standard charts over each nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset U$. Their rings are $R[x]$ and $R[y]$, by the standard-chart statement (a),(c). The ring $R$ is a domain, and the polynomial-domain lemma makes both chart rings domains. These charts are reduced and irreducible. Any two nonempty base affines meet, since $U$ is irreducible; their intersection contains a nonempty affine open $W$. Above $W$, the intersection of either pair of chosen charts contains either $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_U(W)[x]$ or its nonempty principal open where $x$ is invertible. Thus any two covering charts meet. Explicitly, take nonempty opens $O_1,O_2\subset P$ meeting covering charts $C_1,C_2$. Each $C_i$ is irreducible and $C_1\cap C_2$ is a nonempty open in each. Thus $O_1\cap C_1\cap C_2$ and $O_2\cap C_1\cap C_2$ are nonempty opens of the irreducible space $C_1\cap C_2$, so they meet. Also $P$ is nonempty since it contains a domain chart. This proves irreducibility. Every stalk lies on a domain chart and is a localization of a domain, hence reduced; the reduced-and-irreducible criterion gives integrality.

proof.text: Fix one nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset U$. The affine-fraction-field lemma applied to $U$ and $P$ identifies $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $k(P)=\operatorname{Frac}R[x]$ by germs. Inside the latter field, $K$ and $x$ generate it as a field: a fraction of polynomials over $R$ belongs to $K(x)$, and conversely any polynomial over $K$ can have its finitely many coefficient denominators multiplied to give a polynomial over $R$ divided by a nonzero element of $R$. The variable $x$ is transcendental over $K$, since multiplying those denominators in a putative polynomial relation would give a relation in $R[x]$. This gives $k(P)=K(x)$. The constants are the structural pullbacks from $U$, because the chart isomorphisms are $R$-algebra isomorphisms. Surjectivity of $q$ implies dominance. Its generic stalk map gives the specified inclusion $k(P)\hookrightarrow L=k(Y)$, as in the dominant-function-field definition.

source.place: Tags 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions, and 01RW, definition-function-field; explicit fraction calculation

proof.text: The inverse image of the $x$-chart is a nonempty affine open of $Y$ by surjectivity, so the affine-fraction-field lemma gives $L=\operatorname{Frac}S_C$ through the germ embedding. Let $a,b\in L$ be the germs of its displayed coordinates. Their equations are $a^n=x$ and $b^n=x-1$. Every element of $S_C$ is a polynomial in $x,a,b$ over $R$, hence belongs to $K(x)(a,b)$, and therefore so does every quotient of two such elements with nonzero denominator. Conversely $L$ contains $K(x),a,b$. Thus $L=K(x)(a,b)$. The germs agree for different base affines: on a nonempty affine refinement of their intersection the coordinates agree by the assumed restriction compatibility, so they give the same elements of the generic stalk. This also keeps the specified embedding, rather than choosing an abstract field isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; explicit two-root fraction-field calculation

proof.text: Put $F=K(x)$ and consider the subalgebra $B=F[a,b]\subset L$. Replacing each factor $a^n$ by $x$ and $b^n$ by $x-1$ reduces every monomial to an $F$-multiple of $a^ib^j$, $0\leq i,j<n$. These $n^2$ elements span $B$. Since $B$ is a subring of a field it is a domain, and the finite-dimensional-domain lemma makes $B$ a field. It contains $F,a,b$, so it equals $F(a,b)=L$ by the preceding step. Consequently $[L:F]\leq n^2$, in particular the required extension is finite. This uses only $n\geq1$ and does not assert that these monomials are linearly independent.

source.place: Finite algebraic generators: explicit monomial reduction and finite-dimensional-domain argument; Mathlib LinearAlgebra/FiniteDimensional/Basic.lean, FiniteDimensional.exists_mul_eq_one, line 496

proof.text: The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is locally Noetherian: its ring is a field, whose only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. Apply the locally-finite-type Noetherian lemma to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. The presentations in the hypotheses exhibit an affine cover of the inverse image of every base affine by finitely generated $R$-algebras $S_C,S_A$; hence $Y\to U$ is locally of finite type by its definition. Apply the same Noetherian lemma to obtain that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. For either displayed nonempty source chart $T=\operatorname{Spec}S$, apply the normal-sections finite-product lemma to the quasi-compact open $T\subset Y$. It gives $S\cong\prod_{i<r} B_i$ with each $B_i$ an integrally closed domain. Also $S$ is a domain with fraction field $L$ by the affine-fraction-field lemma. Thus $r\ne0$ (the empty product is the zero ring), and $r$ cannot exceed one: two nonzero factors give nonzero complementary idempotents with product zero. Therefore $r=1$ and $S$ is integrally closed in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0358, lemma-normal-integral-sections; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; elementary domain-versus-product argument

proof.text: Apply the finite-normal-cover normalization lemma with $X=P$, $Z=Y$, $f=q$, $F=k(P)=K(x)$, and $L=k(Y)$. Integrality of $P$, finiteness of $L/F$, and local Noetherianity of $Y$ were established above; normality, integrality of $Y$, and finite surjectivity are hypotheses. Its affine conclusion applies to both target charts above every nonempty base affine: their inverse-image rings are precisely the supplied $S_C,S_A$. It identifies each with the integral closure of its target ring in $L$ and gives the compatibility on overlaps and the resulting $P$-isomorphism with the normalization. On the overlap the assumed formulas $y=x^{-1}$, $v=a^{-1}$ and $u=b/a$ are equalities in the same field $L$ (here $a^n=x\ne0$); hence the chart identifications use exactly the displayed coordinates. No extra assumption on $U$, on roots of unity, or on the characteristic has entered the proof.
